newsitem.title: USA: Alaska's Cook Inlet oil-lease area reduced by MMT.
newsitem.headline: Alaska's Cook Inlet oil-lease area reduced by MMT.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service (MMS) on Friday said it was preparing for the sale of oil leases in Alaska's Cook Inlet that would encompass 78 percent less area than originally considered.
The MMS said it prepared an environmental assessment of the revised proposal for the federal Outer Continental Shelf lease sale, which will be subject to a 45-day public comment period.

The area being considered for leasing includes 101 whole and partial blocks of about 43,000 acres, 78 percent less than the 402 blocks on 2 million acres analyzed in MMS' first environmental impact statement.
The sale is tentatively set for April, and final notice will be published at least 30 days before the sale.
Acknowledging the concerns of fishing and environmental interests, the MMS said it was developing additional measures to mitigate the impact of discharged drilling fluids and to protect of fisheries.
The measures would require the oil industry to coordinate activities with participants in commercial, sport and subsistance fishing, and MMS may restrict industry operations.
All planned activities will be reviewed for their potential for affecting various fishing activities.
The MMS said it spent about $2.6 million on environmental and socio-economic studies on the Cook Inlet planning area, including a water-quality study conducted with the University of Alaska.

The area being considered for the lease sale was offered in 1977 and 1981, and MMS issued 100 leases on which companies drilled 13 exploration wells. Those leases expired and the exploration wells were plugged.

All oil and natural gas production in the Cook Inlet area now takes place in state waters above Kalgin Island, where there are 15 production platforms. Daily production amounts to 4,823 barrels of oil and 5,947 thousand cubic feet of natural gas, MMS said.
